verification: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' per URL, and a resolved internal link graph harvested from the homepage

content_urls.note: firecrawl_map did NOT return this page on 2026-10-10 although it is live and in the main nav; on 2026-10-12 the same call DID return it. A single discovery tool's recall is not stable over time, which is a stronger argument for unioning strategies than a fixed blind spot would be. The link graph found it on both dates.
Reachable only as a form-submit destination, so no link graph reaches it. The mirror case of /contact.

must_reject.note: Injected SEO spam with a Japanese product title, still in Google's index. Returned by firecrawl_map.
Harvested from an inline JS template string. A link-graph crawler must restrict hrefs to <a> elements outside <script>.

must_report_not_crawl.note: The hero 'Learn More' button and the 'Meet Dr. Olteanu' card both point here. The real page is /dental-team. Belongs in the redirect map as a decision, not silently repointed.

discovery_strategy_recall.comment: Measured against the 8 content_urls. This is why G-1 requires a union, and it corrects the S2 design in the V3 guide, which proposed firecrawl_map plus a site: search alone. Re-measured 2026-10-12: firecrawl_map returned 8/8 that day, so its recall varies between runs - treat any single strategy's number as a sample, not a constant. Only the union has been 100% on every date measured.

sitemap_only.note: No sitemap at /wp-sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap.xml, /sitemap-index.xml or /page-sitemap.xml; none declared in robots.txt. This is what V2 requires and it returns WP_Error.

firecrawl_map_only.note: 7/8 on 2026-10-10 (missed /contact); 8/8 on 2026-10-12. Not reproducible, so not a fixed blind spot - an unstable one.

link_graph_only.note: 7/8 on both 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-12; the miss is structural.

legacy_url_form.comment: Every internal href is RELATIVE and targets index.html, e.g. href="dental-team/index.html". Both forms serve 200 and no canonical tag exists anywhere, so every page is live at two URLs.
legacy_url_form.requirement: A crawler must resolve relative hrefs against the page base and normalise the index.html form; the legacy form must survive into the redirect map.

remeasurement_note: Re-run on 2026-10-12 with .claude/skills/site-content-harvest/scripts/discover.py --verify: 8/8 content URLs, 3 spam .shtml rejected (the set drifts between runs - one of the original three was absent and a new one appeared), 1 downloadable client document found (/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/New-patient-packet.pdf), and 2 broken internal targets reported: /meet-the-team (403, 5 inbound links from the homepage) and /440.746.9070 (404, a malformed tel link).
